title: Say what you think
line: Give your view clearly, explain it, and make it land.

title: Stand your ground
line: Be firm and confident without being rude: hold a position, set limits, say no.

title: Disagree and debate
line: Push back on the idea, not the person, and argue fairly.

title: Anger and discontent
line: Say exactly how unhappy you are, and why, without losing control.

title: Read what people really mean
line: Spot hints, spin, sarcasm and what is left unsaid.

title: Describe people fairly
line: Words for character: who someone is, not just whether you like them.

title: Name your feelings
line: Say exactly what you feel. Naming it makes it easier to handle.

title: Think clearly
line: Words for reasoning: evidence, bias, assumptions, nuance.

title: Say how sure you are
line: Be exact about certainty. Neither overclaim nor sound unsure of everything.

title: Explain causes and change
line: Why things happen, what follows, and how things grow or fall.

title: Connect your ideas
line: However, whereas, despite: small words that make your logic flow.

title: Work and leading
line: Meetings, emails, teams, decisions, and polite but clear requests.

title: Describe things vividly
line: Places, weather, senses, and how much: stop saying "very".

title: News and society
line: Words for rights, power and public life. No sides taken.

title: Sound natural
line: Phrasal verbs and expressions people really use.
